permitName: Great Sand Dunes National Park Backcountry Permits

addresses.description1: Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve

description.cancellation_policy:
The permit holder may cancel or modify their permit 7 days prior to entry date. The $6.00 reservation fee is non-refundable. Quota from cancelled permits will be immediately released and available on Recreation.gov.   

The permit holder may modify itinerary locations, group size and group member names, emergency contact, or vehicle information prior to printing the permit. Changing the entry date requires a new reservation; reservation fee applies. Once you print your permit, you can no longer make any changes.   

You may request another parking area, 7 or more days in advance; Staff will notify you if your request is granted. There is no guarantee your request will be granted. Your assigned parking lot will be on your printed permit or view your assigned lot from your Recreation.gov account.   

No on-site permits will be available. Changes to vehicle description can be made by the permit holder by writing in new vehicle description information on the printed permit (i.e. rental vehicles).
description.comment_box_description: Please use comment box to request an alternate parking area. Requests are not guaranteed and are based on availability. Requests must be made at least 7 days before the start of your trip. Your final parking location will be viewable on your printed permit.
description.description:
Great Sand Dunes National Park offers two different backpacking experiences – seven designated sites along the Sand Ramp Trail and 20 non-designated sites in the Dunes Backcountry. Backpacking permits are available all year long and provide the visitor with an opportunity to spend the night in unique environments and allows for solitude in the Great Sand Dunes National Park.  

Designated sites along the Sand Ramp Trail are the perfect getaway for backpackers to experience a variety of landscapes - with views of the dunes, amongst mixed conifer forests at the base of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. 

Camping within the tallest dunes in North America is the more popular option for backpackers. The Dunes Backcountry is defined as “west of the high ridge and beyond the day-use area” a minimum distance of 1.5 miles west of the Medano Creek bed.
description.driving_directions:
To reach the designated parking locations shown on the issued permit (Dunes Parking Lot, Horse Trailer Lot, and Amphitheater Parking) drive north on CO State Highway 150 into the park.

By car: 

From Denver, Colorado Springs, or Pueblo, the most common route is south on I-25 to Walsenburg, west on US 160, north on State Highway 150. For a more mountainous drive from Denver (same mileage as the I-25 route), you may also take US 285 south, then State Highway 17 south, then County Lane 6 east from Mosca. 

From Albuquerque, drive north on I-25 to Santa Fe, then north on US 285 to Alamosa. From Alamosa, take either U.S. Highway 160 east and State Highway 150 north, or State Highway 17 north and County Lane 6 east from Mosca.

By air:

Commercial air service is available to a small airport at Alamosa, Colorado, 38 miles from Great Sand Dunes. Colorado Springs, Denver, and Albuquerque are served by many commercial airlines. Rental cars are available at all these airports.
description.fee_policy: Reservation Fee: There is a $6.00 non-refundable reservation fee per permit.
description.need_to_know_email:
Cancellation Policy: The permit holder may cancel their permit 7 days prior to entry date. The $6.00 reservation fee is non-refundable. Quota from cancelled permits will be immediately released and available on Recreation.gov.

Change Policy: The permit holder may modify itinerary locations, group size and group member names, emergency contact, or vehicle information prior to printing the permit. Changing the entry date requires a new reservation for the desired trip date; reservation fee applies.

If permits are reserved the day of the trip, no changes or parking requests will be allowed. No on-site permits or changes will be available.

Permit holder is responsible for knowing the location of their parking area and all rules and regulations. Assigned parking area will be identified on the printed permit, or you can view your assigned parking area from your Recreation.gov account. Permit holder can print the permit and parking pass 7 days in advance of their trip. 

Cold Creek Drainage Stock/Pack Animal Use limited to 6 head of stock between two parties and requires a SEPARATE reservation made at GRSA_permits@nps.gov or at 719-378-6321. Reservations for stock use can be made up to 3 months in advance.
description.need_to_know_order:
All permit holders are responsible for following all the rules and regulations, as well as informing their guests of the rules and regulations.

  • Permit holders can make changes to vehicle description by writing in new vehicle information on the printed permit (i.e. rental vehicles). 
  • Limit of 6 people, 2 vehicles per permit.
  • Dunes Backcountry non-designated sites: Camp beyond the highest ridgeline in any part of the dunefield (with no structures, or roads in sight). Set up camp in low, flat areas away from vegetation. Plan a minimum of 1-hour hiking/climbing to reach the top of the highest ridge, with a view of the entire dunefield. Plan a longer time hiking if you plan to camp beyond the ridgeline above/near Sand Pit or Castle Creek picnic areas. 
  • Sand Ramp Trail designated sites: Camp in designated locations, within 50 feet of the metal arrowhead post. 
  • No trenching around tents.
  • No pets, hammocks, or glass containers.
  • Gas stoves only. No campfires allowed (except in the metal fire ring at Sand Creek designated site). 
  • Pack out trash including food items (orange peels, shells, etc.). 
  • Use a bearproof container or hang food/scented items in a storage bag made from Kevlar in a tree (with rope) at least 10 feet (3m) up and 5 feet (2m) out from the trunk. Campers must use the bear box at the Sand Creek campsite. Dunes backcountry: bear hangs are not required but storing food and scented items in a Kevlar bag will reduce rodents getting into your items.
  • Bury human waste 6 inches deep, 200 feet from water and trails. Pack out toilet paper.  
  • Use privy at Indian Grove or Sand Creek. Pack out toilet paper.
  • Pack animals (horses, mules, burros, donkeys, asses, llamas, alpacas) are allowed overnight in - Dunes Backcountry, Little Medano, Aspen, Cold Creek & Sand Creek. Livestock must be picketed at least 100 feet away from the campsite marker post. Leave-no- Trace principles must be followed where stock is kept overnight to prevent damage to natural or cultural resources
description.need_to_know_permit:
All permit holders are responsible for following all the rules and regulations, as well as informing their guests of the rules and regulations. The following rules and regulations apply: 

• No on-site permits will be available.

• Changes to vehicle description can be made by the permit holder by writing in new vehicle description information on the printed permit (i.e. rental vehicles). 

• Limit of 6 people, 2 vehicles per permit.

• Dunes Backcountry non-designated sites: You must camp beyond the highest ridgeline in any part of the dunefield. If you see any structures, or roads, you have not gone far enough. Set up camp in a low, flat area away from vegetation. Plan a minimum of one-hour hiking/climbing to reach the top of the first ridge, where you will see the entire 30-square-mile dunefield. Plan a longer time hiking if you plan to camp beyond the ridgeline above/near Sand Pit or Castle Creek picnic areas. 

• Sand Ramp Trail designated sites: Camp in designated locations, within 50 feet of the metal arrowhead post. 

• No trenching around tents.

• No pets, hammocks, or glass containers.

• Gas stoves, only. No campfires allowed (except in the metal fire ring at the Sand Creek designated site). 

• Pack out trash including food items such as orange peels and shells. 

• Use a bearproof container or hang food/scented items in a food storage bag made from Kevlar in a tree (with rope) at least 10 feet (3m) up and 5 feet (2m) out from the trunk.
Campers must use the bear box at the Sand Creek campsite. Bear hangs not required in Dunes Backcountry but storing food and other scented items in a bag made from Kevlar will reduce rodents getting into your items.

• Bury human waste 6 inches deep, 200 feet from water and trails. Pack out toilet paper.  

• Use privy at Indian Grove or Sand Creek. Pack out toilet paper.

• Pack animals (horses, mules, burros, donkeys, asses, llamas, alpacas) are allowed in the following areas overnight - Dunes Backcountry, Little Medano, Aspen, Cold Creek and Sand Creek. Livestock must be picketed at least 100 feet away from the campsite marker post. Leave-no- Trace principles must be followed at all locations where stock is kept overnight to prevent damage to natural or cultural resources.

• Check the park website for current conditions, and trip planning tips. 

• Water sources are seasonal. Be prepared to bring water, 1 gallon/person/night is recommended. 

• Boil or treat all stream water before drinking. Water fill up stations are available in the park.

• Sand temperatures may reach 150° F on summer afternoons. Wear closed-toe shoes. 

• Secure tents with sand stakes or sandbags. Strong winds may occur.

• Afternoon thunderstorms are common in warmer months. If lightning threatens, leave the dunes. Crouch low on top of your backpack if you are in immediate danger.
description.quota_details:
The quota for this permit is measured in groups entering per day and number of vehicles per group. 

If quota is available, same-day reservations are possible; there are no first-come, first-served permits available at the park.

Permits are limited to groups of no more than six, and no more than two vehicles per group. The Sand Ramp Trail designated sites allow six people per site. Dunes Backcountry non-designated sites allow for 20 permits/day for groups of no more than six people per permit. Permits may be obtained for a maximum of 14 nights per permit holder.
description.season_information:
Permits are available for advanced reservation year-round on a rolling basis, three months prior to the trip start date at 7:00 am PST/8:00 am MST/10:00 am EST each day.

Permit Options:

  • Dunes Backcountry, non-designated sites: Camp west of the day use area and high ridge line in the dunefield. 
  • Sand Ramp Trail, designated sites: Camp in a designated location, within 50 feet of metal arrowhead post. Sites include: Buck Creek, Escape Dunes, Indian Grove, Little Medano, Aspen, Cold Creek and Sand Creek.

Parking lot assignments are based on the location of the first night’s stay. You may request another parking area, 7 or more days in advance; Great Sand Dunes staff will notify you if your request is granted. Staff cannot guarantee your request will be accommodated. You can view your assigned parking lot on your printed permit or from your Recreation.gov account. If your parking request is granted, you cannot make changes or modifications to your permit.
description.tertiary_page: Permit holders must have emergency contact information listed before the park can issue the permit. The permit holder cannot list themselves or a member of their party as their emergency contact.

467531601.description: This is the most popular and unique backpacking option. Camping is permitted beyond the day use area/west of the highest ridge in the 30-square-mile dunefield. The minimum distance to the backcountry location is approximately 1.5-mile hike from parking area. Enjoy wide open views of the starry sky or a bright moonlit night. Route finding skills are essential for this experience. Locations in the dunefield vary in elevation.

description_map.need_to_know:
It is imperative that backpackers plan for changing conditions no matter what time of year – rain, cold temperatures, heat, hot sand, and bugs. Sand temperatures may reach 150° F on summer afternoons. Wear closed-toe shoes to protect your feet from hot sand. Secure tents with sand stakes or sandbags. Strong winds may occur any time of year. Afternoon thunderstorms are common in warmer months. If lightning threatens, leave the dunes. Crouch low on top of your backpack if you are in immediate danger.

Backpackers must carry 1 gallon of water/person/night as there is no creek to filter from. Campers should avoid camping near high day use areas such as High Dune, or Star Dune and be beyond the ridgecrest visible from the main park road.

467531601.name: Dunes Backcountry

467531602.description: Approximately 0.5 miles north of Loop 2 in the campground. This site is located along a drainage with narrow leaf cottonwood trees and is a short hike into the backcountry. This site is a great option for beginner backpackers. Note: November to March hikers must park in Amphitheater or Horse Trailer Parking Lots since campground access road is closed.

description_map.need_to_know: Buck Creek is a seasonal creek and not a reliable water source. Fill up water at the dunes parking lot or the outdoor spigot at Loop 2 campground restroom facility (April 1 to October 31 Only). During November to March season, stop by visitor center for water filling, open 9 am to 4:30 pm daily.
description_map.site_details: Campground Is closed November 1st to March 31st. Users must park at Point of No Return, Amphitheater, or Horse Trailer Parking during these times.

467531602.name: Buck Creek

467531603.description: Approximately 2.5 miles from the primary parking area. The site is near small "escape dunes," that have left the main dunefield, located in an open grove of ponderosa pines.

description_map.need_to_know:
There is not a reliable water source at this location, pack plenty of water. Fill up water at the dunes parking lot or the outdoor spigot at Loop 2 campground restroom facility. A reliable water source, Medano Creek is located at Creek Crossing 1 along the Medano Pass Primitive Road, approximately 2 miles north of the campsite. Access to this point can be found using the Sand Ramp Trail and Medano Pass Primitive Road.

Take extra caution when filtering from creeks. It is recommended that you place water in a container, let the water settle, then filter from the container. This will prevent water filters from clogging with sand and debris.

467531603.name: Escape Dunes

467531604.description: Approximately 3.9 miles north of the primary parking area. This is the most popular backpacking site because it is close to the main dunefield and close to Medano Creek, in a sheltered grove of narrow leaf cottonwood and pine trees. Visitors are asked to use the privy toilet at the site and pack out all toilet paper.

description_map.need_to_know: Medano Creek flows adjacent to this site. Take extra caution when filtering from creeks. It is recommended that you place water in a container, let the water settle, then filter from the container. This will prevent water filters from clogging with sand and debris.

467531604.name: Indian Grove

467531605.description: Approximately 5.0 miles north of the primary parking area. This site is located in a grove of ponderosa pine trees.

description_map.need_to_know: Little Medano Creek is a reliable water source in most years, located 0.3 mile from the campsite. Medano Creek is 0.5 mile away. Pack plenty of water in case the creeks are dry. Take extra caution when filtering from creeks. It is recommended that you place water in a container, let the water settle, then filter from the container. This will prevent water filters from clogging with sand and debris.

467531605.name: Little Medano

467531606.description: Approximately 6.8 miles north of the primary parking area. This site offers incredible views of the entire dunefield from an aspen grove. At 9,240 feet elevation, it is the highest designated backcountry site in the park. Access to this site from Little Medano requires route finding skills as there is no formal trail between these sites.

description_map.need_to_know: The closest water sources are Little Medano Creek, approximately 1.6 miles away or in Medano Creek, 2.3 miles away. Take extra caution when filtering from creeks. It is recommended that you place water in a container, let the water settle, then filter from the container. This will prevent water filters from clogging with sand and debris.

467531606.name: Aspen

467531607.description: Approximately 10.1 miles from the primary parking area. A destination for the more adventurous backpacker, this site lies in a rugged valley filled with ponderosa pines.

description_map.need_to_know:
Cold Creek is an intermittent creek, an unreliable water source, 300 feet away. Sand Creek is an alternative water source, approximately 1.5 miles away. Pack plenty of water in case the creek is dry. Take extra caution when filtering from creeks. It is recommended that you place water in a container, let the water settle, then filter from the container. This will prevent water filters from clogging with sand and debris. 

Notice of limit on pack animals in the Cold Creek Drainage. No more than two parties with a combined maximum of six(6) head of livestock may be within the watershed of Cold Creek at any one-time. SEPARATE stock use reservations are required by calling 719-378-6321 or email at GRSA_Permits@nps.gov up to 3 months in advance.
description_map.site_details: Stock/Pack Animal Use limited in Cold Creek Drainage and requires SEPARATE reservation at grsa_Permits@nps.gov or 719-378-6321

467531607.name: Cold Creek

467531608.description: Approximately 11.6 miles from the primary parking area. The campsite lies in a beautiful grove of cottonwood trees on the edge of the main dunefield. This site is for the more experienced long-distance hikers and backpackers as the trek to the site is in sand with varying elevation gains. Campers must use the bear box located at the Sand Creek campsite. This is the only backcountry site where campfires are permitted in the national park. Campfires are allowed in the metal fire ring. Collect dead and down wood only. Use water to put the fire out and be certain the fire is out before you leave the site.

description_map.need_to_know: Sand Creek is an intermittent creek, an unreliable water source, located adjacent to the site. Pack plenty of water in case the creek is dry. Take extra caution when filtering from creeks. It is recommended that you place water in a container, let the water settle, then filter from the container. This will prevent water filters from clogging with sand and debris.

467531608.name: Sand Creek
